issues.sym: Clunks or creaks from the front end, the steering pulling to one side, uneven tire wear, or visible rust holes near the front lower control arms.
issues.why: In states that salt their roads, the front subframe rusts from the inside. If it gets bad enough, the lower control arm mount can tear loose, letting the wheel shift into the fender and cutting drive power. Hyundai recalled about 188,000 Sonatas and XGs for this in 2009.
issues.next: Have the subframe inspected right away if you live in the salt belt. Check the VIN for recall 09V-124; the dealer measures the metal and either replaces the subframe or drills drain holes and rust-proofs it for free. A car with a rotted subframe is unsafe to drive.

issues.sym: The airbag (SRS) light comes on at start-up and stays on, or comes and goes. Moving a front seat can trigger it.
issues.why: The most common cause is a loose or strained wiring connector under a front seat, where the harness stretches as the seat moves. Owners also report failed airbag sensors, clock-springs and harnesses.
issues.next: Get the airbag codes read; the airbags may not work while the light is on. Ask the shop to check the connectors under both front seats first, since that is often the simplest fix.

issues.t: Side airbag wiring under seat can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on.
issues.why: The side airbag wiring harness and connector under the front seats can move around, which can turn on the warning light and stop the side airbag from deploying in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 02V-105. The dealer secures the side airbag wiring to the seat frame for free.

issues.t: Engine can stall from engine computer defect (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls, sometimes while driving.
issues.why: A capacitor inside some engine computers (PCMs) was installed incorrectly and can damage the ignition failure sensor, shutting the engine off.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the VIN for recall 01V-362. The dealer checks the computer's build date and replaces it for free if it is affected.

issues.t: Wrong tire pressure label on door (recall)
issues.sym: The tire pressure placard shows the wrong information.
issues.why: Some cars left the factory with an incorrect tire pressure label, which could lead owners to run the wrong pressures.
issues.next: Use the pressures in the owner's manual. Check the VIN for recall 01V-307; Hyundai mails a corrected label for free.

issues.t: Fuel tank valve may leak in a rollover (recall)
issues.why: A valve on the fuel tank may not close fully, so fuel could spill if the car rolls over.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 04V-178. The dealer adds a second fuel tank valve for free.

issues.t: Gas pump keeps clicking off or fuel spits back
issues.sym: The pump nozzle shuts off over and over, so you can only add a little fuel at a time, or fuel splashes back out of the filler.
issues.why: Owners link this to a restricted fuel tank vent or filler neck; the exact cause varies from car to car.
issues.next: Fill slowly with the nozzle at a lower flow setting. Have a shop check the filler neck, tank vent valves and the charcoal (EVAP) canister if it keeps happening.

issues.t: Engine surges or car lunges forward
issues.sym: The engine speeds up on its own, surges when you press the brake, or the car lunges forward while stopped with your foot on the brake.
issues.why: Most NHTSA engine complaints for these cars are filed under speed control. Hyundai issued several updates for the electronic throttle system on these cars, but no single cause has been confirmed.
issues.next: If it happens, press the brake firmly and shift to Neutral. Have a dealer scan for throttle codes, check for throttle-system bulletins and file a report with NHTSA.

issues.t: Check engine light from throttle or accelerator pedal sensor
issues.sym: Check engine light, uneven or weak acceleration, and sometimes a reduced-power mode.
issues.why: The XG350 uses an electronic throttle. Hyundai issued bulletins for throttle system codes and the accelerator position sensor (code P1151), and owners report replacing the throttle position sensor.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A sensor replacement and throttle relearn are common fixes; ask the dealer about the throttle-system bulletins.

issues.t: Check engine light for lean codes P0171 / P0174
issues.sym: Check engine light, sometimes with a rough idle or hesitation.
issues.why: Both sides of the V6 are running lean, usually from an air leak at the intake or vacuum hoses, a dirty airflow sensor, or weak fuel delivery. Hyundai issued a bulletin for these codes on 2001–2005 XG300 and XG350.
issues.next: Have a shop smoke-test the intake for leaks and check the airflow sensor and fuel pressure before replacing parts.

issues.t: Rough idle from faulty EGR switching valve
issues.sym: The idle is rough or unsteady, on and off.
issues.why: A faulty exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) switching valve can let exhaust into the intake at the wrong time. Hyundai issued an EGR diagnosis bulletin.
issues.next: Have the EGR switching valve and its hoses tested.

issues.t: Harsh, delayed or erratic automatic shifting
issues.sym: Hard or late shifts, the car lurching when you put it in Drive, slipping, or the transmission getting stuck in one gear.
issues.why: Many complaints trace back to old transmission computer software, the wrong fluid, or adaptive settings that need a relearn; worn clutches cause the rest. Hyundai issued bulletins for software, relearning and solenoid codes.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid level and type checked. Ask for a software check and adaptive relearn before agreeing to a rebuild.

issues.t: Transmission oil leak at reduction brake piston cover
issues.sym: Reddish fluid drips under the front of the car, near the transmission.
issues.why: Hyundai bulletin 0640004 covers an oil leak at the reduction brake piston cover on the 2005 XG350's transmission.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and have the cover's seal replaced before the level gets low.
issues.sevReason: Rule false positive: a transmission band ("reduction brake") seal leak, not the wheel brakes.

issues.t: Timing belt wear and slipped timing
issues.sym: Usually no warning. A belt that is old, slipped or broken can cause a rough run, a no-start, or the engine stopping suddenly.
issues.why: These V6 engines use a rubber timing belt that must be replaced on schedule. If it breaks or jumps a tooth the valves can hit the pistons; mechanics also report belts slipping after a poor installation.
issues.next: Check your records. If there is no proof of a belt change within the owner's manual interval, replace the belt, tensioner and usually the water pump together at a shop that has done this engine before.

issues.t: Cranks but won't start (crank sensor or reluctor)
issues.sym: The engine cranks normally but will not start, often with no codes.
issues.why: A failed crankshaft position sensor is a common cause. After timing belt work, the sensor's reluctor (trigger wheel) on the crank sprocket can slip and throw off spark timing.
issues.next: Have a shop check spark and the crank sensor signal before replacing parts, especially if the timing belt was just done.

issues.sym: The engine revs very high right after a cold start before settling down.
issues.why: One owner's dealer replaced the crank sensor, accelerator sensor and a valve without fixing it; idle and throttle control faults are the usual cause.
issues.next: Have the idle and throttle system scanned while the problem is happening and ask about Hyundai's throttle-system bulletins.

issues.t: Clunk or grinding from torn CV axle boots
issues.sym: Clicking when turning, a clunk when pulling away, or grease sprayed inside the wheel.
issues.why: The rubber boot on a front axle can split, letting grease out and dirt in, which wears out the CV joint.
issues.next: Have the boots inspected. Replacing a torn boot early can prevent replacing the axle.

issues.t: A/C stops cooling on long drives
issues.sym: Cold air turns warm after an hour or so of driving, then works again after the fan is turned off for a while.
issues.why: Owners report this but no single cause has been confirmed; a shop typically checks the refrigerant charge, the evaporator temperature sensor and the A/C relay.
issues.next: Have the A/C system tested while the problem is happening.

issues.t: Seat belt warning light stays on
issues.sym: The seat belt reminder light stays on even with belts buckled.
issues.why: Owners report it without a confirmed cause; a faulty buckle switch or loose wiring under the seat is the usual suspect.
issues.next: Have the buckle switch and under-seat connectors checked.
